title: Attendance Policy – TechVerse University
content:
Attendance Policy – TechVerse University

TechVerse University recognizes that regular classroom participation is fundamental to academic excellence. All students enrolled in undergraduate and postgraduate engineering programs are expected to maintain a minimum attendance of 75 percent in each registered course, including theory lectures, laboratory sessions, tutorials, and project hours, throughout every semester.

Minimum Attendance Requirement

Students must secure at least 75 percent attendance in every individual subject. Attendance is calculated separately for each course and is not averaged across subjects. A student who meets the 75 percent threshold in most subjects but falls short in even one course will be declared ineligible for the end-semester examination in that particular subject. The university emphasizes that attendance is tracked from the first working day of the semester, and late admissions or registration delays do not grant retroactive exemptions unless approved in writing by the Dean of Academic Affairs.

Examination Eligibility Based on Attendance

Students whose attendance in any course falls below 65 percent will be declared ineligible to appear in the end-semester examination for that course under any circumstances. No condonation, medical certificate, or special appeal can override this strict cutoff. Students falling below 65 percent must re-register for the course in the subsequent semester and attend it fresh.

Students whose attendance falls within the range of 65 percent to 74 percent may apply for attendance condonation. Condonation is not a right but a privilege granted under exceptional circumstances. Valid reasons considered for condonation include hospitalization supported by medical documentation, participation in inter-university sports events or technical fests with prior institutional approval, bereavement, or representation of the university in government-recognized activities. Students seeking condonation must submit a formal application to the Department Head within seven working days of the issue arising, accompanied by relevant supporting documents. The final decision rests with the Academic Condonation Committee, which meets bi-weekly.

Tracking and Notification

Attendance is updated on the university's Student Information Portal (SIP) within 48 hours of every class. Students are urged to monitor their attendance weekly. The university issues automated alerts via the registered email and SMS when a student's attendance in any subject drops to 80 percent, serving as an early warning. Faculty coordinators are required to display consolidated attendance records on departmental notice boards at the end of every month.

Leave and Absence Management

All planned absences, such as those for medical treatment or family emergencies, must be communicated to the class advisor in advance or within two working days of return. Unauthorized prolonged absence of more than ten consecutive working days without intimation may result in disciplinary action as defined under the Student Discipline Policy. Medical leave supported by a registered medical practitioner's certificate may be considered during condonation evaluation but does not automatically restore attendance percentage.

Laboratory and Practical Attendance

Laboratory and practical sessions carry separate attendance records. A student must complete all assigned lab experiments and secure at least 75 percent lab attendance to be eligible for the practical examination. Missed lab sessions can be compensated only through pre-approved makeup sessions scheduled by the respective faculty member. No makeup is guaranteed, and it remains at the faculty's discretion.

Special Cases and Appeals

Students representing TechVerse University in national-level competitions, cultural events, or academic delegations are entitled to treat those days as duty leave, which counts toward attendance. However, prior permission from the Head of Department and submission of participation proof is mandatory. Appeals against attendance decisions must be submitted to the Academic Grievance Cell within 15 days of semester-end attendance publication.

title: Examination & Evaluation Policy – TechVerse University
content:
Examination & Evaluation Policy – TechVerse University

TechVerse University follows a continuous and comprehensive evaluation system designed to assess students across multiple dimensions of learning throughout the semester. The academic assessment framework is structured to reflect both consistent effort and conceptual mastery, ensuring that no single examination determines a student's academic standing entirely.

Evaluation Structure

Each theory course is evaluated for a total of 100 marks. The internal assessment component constitutes 40 marks and the end-semester examination accounts for 60 marks. The internal assessment includes two cycle tests of 10 marks each, one model examination worth 15 marks, and assignment or quiz components worth the remaining 5 marks. Practical and laboratory courses are assessed separately based on observation records, viva voce examinations, and practical performance, totaling 100 marks with a defined internal-to-external split specified in each course syllabus.

Grading and CGPA System

TechVerse University employs a 10-point Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) system. Letter grades are awarded based on the total marks secured in each course: O (Outstanding) for 91–100, A+ for 81–90, A for 71–80, B+ for 61–70, B for 51–60, and RA (Reappearance Required) for marks below 50. CGPA is computed at the end of every semester based on the credits assigned to each course and the grade points earned. Students must secure a minimum passing mark of 50 in both the internal assessment and end-semester examination independently. Passing only one component does not constitute a pass in the course.

Arrears and Re-examination Policy

A student who fails to secure the minimum passing marks in a course is said to have an arrear in that subject. Students can accumulate arrears across semesters, but the arrear count directly impacts academic progression and placement eligibility. Students with more than two active arrears are not permitted to sit for semester promotions in certain programs and may face restrictions on elective course registration. Arrear examinations are conducted at the end of each academic semester during the supplementary examination window. A student may attempt to clear an arrear any number of times, but the maximum grade achievable for an arrear paper cleared after the first attempt is B, irrespective of marks scored.

End-Semester Examination Conduct

The end-semester examinations are conducted by the Office of the Controller of Examinations. The examination schedule is published at least four weeks before the commencement of examinations. Students must carry their hall ticket, which is issued only upon clearing all outstanding dues to the university including fees and library fines, and upon meeting the 75 percent attendance requirement. Malpractice during examinations, including possession of unauthorized materials, communication with other students, or impersonation, will result in cancellation of the examination paper and may lead to further disciplinary action including suspension or debarment from future examinations.

Model Examination Policy

The model examination serves as a preparatory assessment and is conducted internally by the department approximately three weeks before the end-semester examination. Attendance in the model examination is compulsory. Students who miss the model examination without a valid prior-approved reason will receive zero marks for that component, which will be carried over to the internal assessment total.

Results and Revaluation

End-semester examination results are published on the Student Information Portal within 30 working days of the last examination date. Students who are dissatisfied with their results may apply for photocopy of their answer sheet within 10 days of result publication by paying the prescribed fee. A revaluation request may subsequently be submitted within seven days of receiving the photocopy. Revaluation is a one-time process and the marks awarded after revaluation, whether higher or lower than the original, are final and binding.

title: Fees & Scholarship Policy – TechVerse University
content:
Fees & Scholarship Policy – TechVerse University

TechVerse University is committed to ensuring that financial constraints do not hinder deserving students from accessing quality engineering education. The university has established a transparent fee structure along with a robust scholarship ecosystem that recognizes academic merit, athletic achievement, and genuine financial need.

Fee Structure and Payment Schedule

The annual tuition fee for undergraduate B.Tech programs is structured into two semester-wise installments. The first installment is due before the commencement of the odd semester, and the second installment is due before the even semester begins. Students are expected to pay fees through the university's online payment portal using net banking, UPI, or demand draft. Late payment of fees beyond the due date attracts a fine of rupees 100 per day for the first 10 days, after which the student's access to the Student Information Portal, library, and hostel facilities may be temporarily suspended. Fees once paid are non-refundable except in cases of withdrawal before the academic year begins, subject to the refund policy outlined by the university.

Merit Scholarship

The TechVerse Merit Scholarship is awarded at the beginning of each academic year to students who have demonstrated outstanding academic performance in the preceding year. Eligibility criteria require the student to have secured a CGPA of 8.5 or above in the previous academic year with zero active arrears. The scholarship covers 50 percent of the tuition fee for the subsequent year. Students must reapply each year and meet the updated eligibility criteria. The scholarship is tenable only for the standard duration of the program and cannot be extended beyond the program's prescribed completion period.

Sports Scholarship

Recognizing the importance of holistic development, TechVerse University offers the Sports Excellence Scholarship to students who have represented their state or the country in recognized sports disciplines at the national or international level. Applicants must provide documentation from the relevant sports authority at the time of application. The Sports Scholarship covers 25 percent of the tuition fee and may be combined with the Merit Scholarship subject to the approval of the Scholarship Review Committee. Sports scholars are expected to represent the university in institutional-level sports events during their tenure.

Financial Assistance Program

Students from economically disadvantaged backgrounds may apply for the TechVerse Financial Assistance Program. Eligibility is determined based on family income, which must not exceed rupees five lakh per annum as per the latest income certificate issued by a competent government authority. Applicants must submit the income certificate, ration card or equivalent document, and a personal statement of need. Financial assistance may cover up to 75 percent of tuition fees and is reviewed annually. Students receiving financial assistance must maintain a minimum CGPA of 6.0 and have no active disciplinary proceedings against them.

Government Scholarships and Liaison

TechVerse University actively facilitates applications for government-sponsored scholarships including the Post-Matric Scholarship for SC/ST students, the Central Sector Scheme for top-merit students, and state-level scholarship programs. The Scholarship Cell under the Office of Student Affairs assists students in completing documentation, verifying eligibility, and submitting applications through the relevant government portals. Students are advised to approach the Scholarship Cell at the start of each academic year to avoid missing application deadlines.

Fee Waiver for Institutional Representatives

Students who are officially nominated to represent TechVerse University in national-level technical competitions, cultural festivals, or inter-university events may apply for a partial fee waiver for the semester in which the event occurs. Applications must be supported by nomination letters from the respective student activity club advisor and approved by the Dean of Student Affairs. All fee-related grievances must be addressed to the Accounts Office in writing within 15 days of the contested transaction.

title: Placement & Career Services Policy – TechVerse University
content:
Placement & Career Services Policy – TechVerse University

TechVerse University's Training and Placement Cell (TPC) is dedicated to bridging the gap between academic preparation and industry employment. The TPC manages all aspects of campus recruitment, career readiness training, and employer relationship management to ensure that TechVerse graduates are equipped and positioned for meaningful professional careers.

Eligibility Criteria for Campus Placements

To participate in campus placement drives conducted or facilitated by the TPC, students must meet specific academic eligibility conditions. A minimum Cumulative Grade Point Average of 7.0, calculated from the first semester through the most recently completed semester, is required. In addition, students must have no more than two active arrears at the time of sitting for any company's written test or interview process. Students who have more than two arrears are advised to clear them before the placement season commences, typically in the sixth semester for final year students. CGPA is verified at the time of registration and again at the time of offer letter issuance; any discrepancy may lead to disqualification from the placement process.

Placement Registration and Process

Students interested in participating in campus placements must register with the TPC at the start of their seventh semester through the Placement Portal. Registration requires submission of an updated resume, official academic transcripts, and a signed declaration of placement intent. Once registered, students will receive notifications about company visits, pre-placement talks, online assessments, and interview schedules. It is mandatory to attend all company sessions for which a student has registered. Unexcused absences from company visits after registration will be treated as a breach of placement norms and may result in temporary suspension from future placement activities.

Dream and Super Dream Companies

The TPC classifies recruiting organizations into three tiers based on compensation offered: Standard, Dream, and Super Dream. Students who have already received an offer from a Standard company may continue to sit for Dream and Super Dream companies. Once a student receives an offer from a Dream company, they may sit for Super Dream companies only, but participation in Standard drives is discontinued. Upon receiving a Super Dream offer, the student is considered placed and must withdraw from all further drives. This policy ensures equitable opportunities for unplaced students.

Pre-Placement Training

From the fifth semester onward, the TPC conducts structured pre-placement training covering aptitude reasoning, verbal communication, technical domains, group discussion facilitation, and mock interview sessions. Attendance in pre-placement training sessions is strongly encouraged and is mandatory for students with a CGPA below 7.5, who are categorized as priority candidates requiring additional preparation support. The TPC also coordinates with external training agencies and industry professionals to deliver domain-specific bootcamps in areas such as software development, data science, core engineering, and management consulting.

Higher Studies and Off-Campus Support

Students who choose to pursue higher studies including GATE, GRE, GMAT, CAT, or professional certifications are supported through a dedicated Higher Studies Advisory Program. The TPC maintains a resource library of previous years' examination papers, study guides, and access to digital learning subscriptions. For students seeking off-campus employment, the TPC shares relevant job postings, assists with resume review, and provides reference letters upon request from the department.

Conduct and Ethics During Placement

All students participating in campus recruitment are expected to maintain the highest standards of professional conduct. Any form of misrepresentation of academic credentials, fraudulent documentation, or disrespectful behavior during company interactions will result in immediate disqualification from the current and future placement cycles and may be reported to the company and escalated to the Discipline Committee.

title: Internship & Industrial Training Policy – TechVerse University
content:
Internship & Industrial Training Policy – TechVerse University

Internships and industrial training form an essential component of the engineering curriculum at TechVerse University. The university firmly believes that real-world industry exposure during the course of academic study enables students to apply theoretical knowledge, build professional skills, and develop workplace readiness. Accordingly, internship participation is mandatory for all students enrolled in undergraduate engineering programs.

Mandatory Internship Requirement

Every student pursuing a B.Tech degree at TechVerse University must complete at least one internship during the course of their program. The minimum duration of an acceptable internship is six weeks, equivalent to approximately 30 working days of full-time engagement. Part-time internships or internships undertaken during the regular academic semester without prior approval are generally not recognized for credit. Internships are primarily intended to be completed during the summer break following the completion of the fourth or sixth semester, though exceptions for other periods may be approved on a case-by-case basis by the Department Internship Coordinator.

Internship Approval Process

Before commencing an internship, students are required to obtain prior approval from their Department Internship Coordinator. A formal internship request form, along with the offer letter or engagement letter from the prospective organization, must be submitted at least one week before the proposed start date. Organizations offering internships must be registered entities with a verifiable presence. Internships at startup organizations are accepted provided the company is incorporated and a faculty mentor is assigned for co-supervision. Self-declared or family business internships are evaluated on a case-by-case basis and require enhanced documentation and periodic progress reports.

Documentation and Credit Earning

Upon completion of the internship, students must submit a comprehensive internship report within 15 days of return to the university. The report must include an executive summary, description of the organization, detailed account of work performed, learnings and reflections, and an acknowledgment letter on the organization's letterhead signed by the supervising manager or engineer. Credits for the internship are awarded only upon satisfactory evaluation of the report by a departmental panel and the submission of an attendance or work completion certificate from the host organization. The internship carries a defined credit weight as specified in the respective program's curriculum framework.

Stipend and Remote Internships

While the university encourages students to seek paid internships, the presence or absence of a stipend does not affect the academic recognition of the internship. Remote and virtual internships gained recognition following their widespread adoption and are acceptable provided the student can demonstrate substantive task completion and the host organization confirms engagement. Remote internships must involve a minimum of four hours of active work per day throughout the stipulated duration.

Internship Through Training and Placement Cell

The TPC facilitates internship opportunities by connecting students with partner organizations. Students who secure internships through TPC-facilitated channels must follow the same documentation process but receive additional support in the form of faculty mentoring, mid-internship progress reviews, and employer feedback collection. Students are encouraged but not obligated to use TPC channels; self-sourced internships are equally recognized.

Consequences of Non-Compliance

Students who fail to complete the mandatory internship requirement by the time they reach the final year will have an academic hold placed on their registration for the seventh semester until the internship obligation is fulfilled or a formal deferral is approved. In exceptional cases, such as health emergencies or personal crises, the Dean of Academic Affairs may grant a structured deferral, requiring the internship to be completed in a manner compatible with the final year schedule. Non-submission of internship documentation without approved deferral will result in the course appearing as an arrear on the student's transcript.

title: Hostel & Residential Rules – TechVerse University
content:
Hostel & Residential Rules – TechVerse University

TechVerse University provides on-campus residential facilities for students from outstation locations, prioritizing students from other states and those whose permanent residence is more than 50 kilometers from the campus. The university hostels are designed to provide a safe, disciplined, and comfortable living environment that supports academic focus and personal well-being.

Allotment and Eligibility

Hostel accommodation is not automatically guaranteed to all students. Allotment is made based on distance from hometown, availability of rooms, and academic year, with first-year students generally given priority to support their transition to campus life. Applications for hostel accommodation must be submitted online through the Student Information Portal before the stipulated deadline, which is typically 30 days before the start of the academic year. Allotments are communicated via email and are subject to the availability of the gender-appropriate hostel block.

Curfew and Movement Rules

All hostel residents are required to be present within their respective hostel premises by 9:30 PM on all days including weekends. This curfew is enforced strictly through biometric check-in systems installed at hostel entry points. Students who need to return after curfew for documented academic reasons such as laboratory projects, institutional events, or official university duties must obtain a written gate pass from the Hostel Warden at least two hours before the curfew time. Repeated violations of the curfew rule, defined as three or more violations per semester, will result in escalation to the Discipline Committee and may lead to hostel eviction.

Room Conduct and Hygiene Standards

Students are expected to maintain cleanliness within their rooms and common areas at all times. Rooms are subject to inspection by the Warden or Resident Advisor on any day without prior notice. Students found maintaining unhygienic conditions will receive a formal warning, and persistent violations may affect hostel renewal for the subsequent year. Cooking inside hostel rooms using electric coils, gas stoves, or any open-flame equipment is strictly prohibited due to fire safety regulations. Possession of such equipment will result in immediate confiscation and a formal notice.

Guest and Visitor Policy

Outsiders are not permitted inside hostel residential blocks under any circumstances. Visitors including parents and guardians may meet residents only in the designated visitor lounge located at the hostel reception area and only between 10:00 AM and 6:00 PM on weekdays and 9:00 AM and 7:00 PM on weekends. Students wishing to bring a visitor to campus must inform the warden in advance and ensure the visitor signs the visitor register. Day scholars are not permitted inside the residential blocks of hostels.

Hostel Fees and Deposits

Hostel fees cover accommodation, dining hall access, and basic utilities. These fees are billed separately from academic tuition fees and must be paid along with the semester fee installment. A refundable caution deposit is collected at the time of first allotment and is returned upon vacating the hostel after deducting any damage charges as assessed during the exit inspection. Students who vacate mid-semester without prior notice to the Warden forfeit their deposit.

Discipline and Eviction

Behavior that disturbs fellow residents, including loud noise after quiet hours which begin at 10:30 PM, harassment, ragging of any kind, possession of alcohol, tobacco, or any prohibited substances, and unauthorized possession of another student's belongings, constitutes serious misconduct. Any such behavior is subject to immediate disciplinary action as outlined in the Student Discipline Policy. The Chief Warden holds the authority to recommend hostel eviction for severe or repeated violations, and such cases are reviewed by the Hostel Discipline Panel within seven working days of the incident.

title: Library & Digital Learning Policy – TechVerse University
content:
Library & Digital Learning Policy – TechVerse University

The TechVerse University Central Library is the intellectual hub of the campus, providing students, faculty, and research scholars with access to a vast and curated collection of print and digital academic resources. The library is committed to supporting learning, research, and innovation through well-organized services and inclusive access policies.

Library Membership and Access

All currently enrolled students are automatically registered as library members upon confirmation of admission. Library membership provides access to the physical library space, the borrowing service, and the university's digital library subscription portal. Library identity cards, which are required for borrowing books, are issued through the library office within the first two weeks of the academic year. Loss of the library card must be reported immediately, and a replacement can be obtained by paying the prescribed replacement fee.

Book Borrowing Policy

Students are permitted to borrow a maximum of five books simultaneously from the Central Library. Each borrowed book carries a loan period of 14 days, which may be renewed online through the library portal for an additional 14 days, provided no reservation request has been placed by another user for the same title. A student may renew a book a maximum of two times consecutively. Overdue books attract a fine of rupees two per day per book beyond the due date. Students with pending library dues exceeding rupees 200 will have their borrowing privileges suspended until the outstanding amount is cleared.

Reference and Reserved Collections

Certain textbooks, reference volumes, and journal collections are designated as reference-only or reserved-section materials and cannot be borrowed for home use. These materials are available for in-library use during library hours. Photocopying of reference materials is permitted within the limits of copyright regulations and only through the library's self-service photocopy facility.

Digital Library and Online Resources

TechVerse University subscribes to multiple digital databases and academic publishing platforms including IEEE Xplore, Elsevier ScienceDirect, Springer, NPTEL, and the National Digital Library of India. Access to these platforms is available on-campus through the university network without individual login. Off-campus access is enabled through the university's VPN service, for which students must register using their institutional email credentials through the IT Services portal. Students are advised not to share their digital library login credentials, as individual access logs are monitored and misuse may lead to suspension of digital library privileges.

Library Conduct and Decorum

The library is a space for focused academic work. Students must maintain complete silence in the reading halls. Mobile phones must be kept on silent mode, and phone calls are not permitted inside the library premises. Food and beverages are strictly prohibited within the library building. Students are expected to return books and study materials to their correct shelves or book-return trolleys after use and must not rearrange shelves independently.

Special Services and Study Rooms

The Central Library provides access to 12 individual study carrels and four group study rooms, all of which can be reserved up to 48 hours in advance through the library portal. Group study rooms can accommodate up to six students and are available for two-hour sessions, extendable by one hour if unoccupied. Extended library hours during the pre-examination period are announced each semester. The library also offers interlibrary loan services in collaboration with partner institutions, allowing students to access titles not available in the TechVerse collection within 7 to 10 working days of request.

title: Final Year Project Guidelines – TechVerse University
content:
Final Year Project Guidelines – TechVerse University

The Final Year Project (FYP) is the culminating academic experience of the undergraduate engineering program at TechVerse University. It offers students the opportunity to apply their accumulated knowledge and skills to address a real-world problem, conduct original research, or develop a functional technical prototype. The FYP spans the seventh and eighth semesters and carries significant credit weight in the final year curriculum.

Project Selection and Approval

Students are required to identify their project area and propose a topic by the end of the fourth week of the seventh semester. Each project must have a faculty mentor from the student's department, and mentorship assignments are finalized during the project allocation meeting held by the Department Project Coordinator. Students may propose a project conceived independently or choose from a list of faculty-recommended and industry-suggested topics available on the department notice board. All project proposals must be submitted via the Project Management Portal and receive explicit written approval from the assigned mentor before any substantive work begins. Unapproved projects will not be eligible for credit evaluation.

Plagiarism Policy

TechVerse University enforces a strict academic integrity standard for all final year projects. The project report submitted at the end of the eighth semester must not contain more than 15 percent similarity as detected by the university's licensed plagiarism detection software. Reports with a similarity index between 15 and 25 percent will be returned for mandatory revision and resubmission before the final evaluation date. Reports exceeding 25 percent similarity will be rejected outright, and the student will be required to substantially rework and resubmit, with a consequential delay in degree conferral. Deliberate plagiarism or manipulation of the similarity report constitutes serious academic misconduct and will be referred to the Discipline Committee.

Project Report Structure and Submission

The final project report must adhere to the formatting guidelines published by the Office of Academic Affairs. The report must include an abstract, introduction, literature review, methodology, results and analysis, conclusion, and references formatted in IEEE citation style. A signed declaration of originality, certified by the faculty mentor and the Head of Department, must accompany every submitted report. Submission is accepted only through the Project Portal as a PDF document, along with a bound hard copy to be deposited with the department library. The deadline for final submission is communicated at the beginning of the eighth semester, and late submissions attract a penalty of grade capping at B+ unless a formal extension has been approved.

Progress Reviews and Presentations

Each project team, which may consist of one to three students unless otherwise specified by the department, is required to participate in three formal review presentations during the project lifecycle. The first review is held at the end of the seventh semester and focuses on the project proposal and literature survey. The second review at the midpoint of the eighth semester evaluates methodology and preliminary results. The final presentation before a panel of internal and external examiners constitutes the major evaluation component. Attendance at all three reviews is compulsory, and absence from any review without prior approval from the mentor will result in a deduction of marks from the internal assessment component.

Industry and External Collaboration

Students are encouraged to take up projects in collaboration with industry partners, research institutions, or NGOs. Industry-mentored projects must have both an industry supervisor and an assigned faculty co-mentor. Confidentiality agreements requested by industry partners are permissible provided the project outcome can still be evaluated academically. Any intellectual property arising from such projects is governed by the university's IP Policy and a shared agreement with the collaborating organization.

title: Student Discipline & Grievance Policy – TechVerse University
content:
Student Discipline & Grievance Policy – TechVerse University

TechVerse University is committed to maintaining a campus environment that upholds dignity, safety, academic integrity, and mutual respect. The Student Discipline and Grievance Policy outlines the standards of conduct expected from all students and establishes fair and transparent mechanisms for addressing misconduct and resolving student grievances.

Code of Conduct

All students of TechVerse University are expected to conduct themselves with integrity, professionalism, and respect toward fellow students, faculty, administrative staff, and university property at all times. Academic misconduct, which includes cheating during examinations, plagiarism in assignments or project reports, fabrication of data, and impersonation, is treated with the utmost seriousness. Social misconduct, including ragging, harassment of any form (including sexual, verbal, and cyberbullying), discrimination based on gender, caste, religion, or regional identity, and any act of violence or intimidation, constitutes a severe breach of the university's code of conduct.

Anti-Ragging Policy

TechVerse University maintains a zero-tolerance policy toward ragging in any form, consistent with the directives of the Supreme Court of India and the University Grants Commission. Ragging is defined broadly to include any act that causes or is likely to cause embarrassment, physical, psychological, or social harm to any student, particularly new entrants. All students are required to submit a signed anti-ragging undertaking at the time of admission. Verified complaints of ragging will be investigated by the Anti-Ragging Committee and may result in expulsion from the university, cancellation of hostel accommodation, and legal action as warranted.

Disciplinary Procedure

Complaints regarding student misconduct may be submitted to the Student Discipline Committee (SDC) through the Dean of Student Affairs' office or via the secure online complaint portal available on the university website. Upon receipt of a complaint, the SDC will issue a notice to the concerned student within three working days and conduct a preliminary inquiry. The student will be given a fair opportunity to present their version of events either in writing or in person before the committee. Disciplinary actions, graduated according to the severity of the offense, include formal warnings, fine imposition, suspension from academic activities, cancellation of hostel accommodation, debarment from placement activities, and in extreme cases, rustication or permanent expulsion.

Grievance Redressal Mechanism

Students who experience academic or administrative grievances, including disputes over attendance records, examination results, fee-related issues, or unfair treatment by faculty or staff, may file a formal grievance through the Student Grievance Cell. The Grievance Cell operates under the Office of the Ombudsperson and ensures complete confidentiality of the complainant's identity where requested. All grievances must be submitted within 30 days of the occurrence of the issue. The Grievance Cell is mandated to acknowledge receipt within 48 hours and resolve or escalate the matter within 15 working days.

Sexual Harassment and Internal Complaints Committee

In compliance with the Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal of Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act 2013, TechVerse University has constituted an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC). The ICC is chaired by a senior female faculty member and includes student representatives and an external member from an NGO. Students experiencing sexual harassment are encouraged to approach the ICC directly, and all complaints are handled with confidentiality and sensitivity. Retaliatory action against a complainant is itself treated as a punishable offense.

Appeals

Students aggrieved by the decision of the SDC or Grievance Cell may appeal to the University Appeals Committee, chaired by the Vice Chancellor or a designated senior authority, within 14 days of receiving the written decision. The appeals process is final and binding.

title: Campus IT & Student Support Services – TechVerse University
content:
Campus IT & Student Support Services – TechVerse University

TechVerse University's Information Technology infrastructure is designed to provide students with seamless connectivity, access to digital academic resources, and comprehensive support throughout their university journey. The Office of IT Services manages all technology infrastructure on campus and is supported by a dedicated student helpdesk team.

Campus Wi-Fi and Network Access

High-speed Wi-Fi connectivity is available across all academic buildings, the central library, administrative blocks, student activity centers, and hostel premises. Students can access the campus wireless network using their institutional login credentials, which are issued during the registration process at the beginning of each academic year. The campus network operates on a bandwidth-managed system that prioritizes academic traffic. Misuse of the network for downloading pirated content, accessing prohibited websites, or engaging in activities that violate the university's Acceptable Use Policy will result in immediate suspension of network access and may invite disciplinary action.

Student Information Portal (SIP)

The Student Information Portal is the central digital platform for all academic and administrative interactions. Through the SIP, students can view and download their attendance records, examination results, fee payment receipts, course materials uploaded by faculty, academic calendars, and hall tickets. Students can also apply for bonafide certificates, transcripts, and other official documents through the SIP. It is the student's responsibility to keep their SIP profile updated with a valid email address and mobile number to ensure receipt of critical notifications.

VPN and Off-Campus Access

Students who require access to the university's digital library subscriptions, the SIP, or institutional email from off-campus locations can do so by connecting through the university's Virtual Private Network (VPN) service. VPN credentials are issued upon request through the IT Services portal and are tied to the student's institutional email account. VPN access is restricted to one active device per student account. Any suspected misuse or sharing of VPN credentials will be investigated and may result in access revocation.

Institutional Email and Software Access

Each student is assigned an official TechVerse University email account in the format studentid@techverse.edu.in upon admission. This email serves as the primary channel for all official communications from the university including examination notifications, fee reminders, placement alerts, and policy updates. Students are expected to check their institutional email at least once daily. Additionally, students have access to institutional software licenses for tools including MATLAB, AutoCAD, Microsoft Office 365, and various simulation packages through the IT Services portal, available for installation on personal devices.

IT Helpdesk and Support

The IT Helpdesk is located at the ground floor of the Main Academic Block and is operational from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM on working days. Students can raise IT support tickets for issues including Wi-Fi connectivity problems, SIP login difficulties, software installation support, hardware issues in computer labs, and email access problems. Support requests can also be submitted via the helpdesk email or through the SIP's built-in ticket system. Standard response time for helpdesk tickets is four working hours for priority issues and one working day for routine requests.

Cyber Safety and Digital Literacy

The university conducts mandatory cyber safety orientation sessions for all first-year students during their induction week. These sessions cover responsible internet use, phishing awareness, data privacy, safe use of social media, and the implications of cybercrime under Indian law. Students are strongly discouraged from sharing sensitive academic credentials on any third-party website. Any cybersecurity incidents, including suspected account compromises or phishing attempts, must be reported immediately to the IT Security Cell at security@techverse.edu.in for prompt investigation and remediation.
